src.text:
INTRODUCTION (what the novel is, who wrote it, when):
Alice's Adventures in Wonderland (also known as  Alice in Wonderland) is an 1865 English children's novel by Lewis Carroll. It tells the story of a little girl named Alice who falls through a rabbit hole into a fantasy world of anthropomorphic creatures. It is seen as an example of the literary nonsense genre. The artist John Tenniel provided 42 wood-engraved illustrations for the original edition.
The novel received positive reviews upon release. It has become one of the best-known works of Victorian literature; its narrative, structure, characters, and imagery have had a wide influence on popular culture and literature, especially in the fantasy genre. It is credited as helping end an era of didacticism in children's literature, inaugurating an era in which writing for children aimed to "delight or entertain". The tale plays with logic, giving the story lasting popularity with adults a

PLOT (an editor-reviewed concise summary of the whole story, 787 words; the ONLY source of the events):
Sitting with her older sister on a bank, and feeling rather sleepy and bored, Alice suddenly spots a White Rabbit with a pocket watch and waistcoat hurrying by, lamenting that he is late. Surprised, Alice follows him down a rabbit hole, which sends her into a lengthy fall. Landing safely, she finds herself inside a room where she discovers a key to a tiny door, beyond which is a garden. While pondering how to fit through the door, she notices a bottle labelled "Drink me". Alice drinks some of the contents and, to her astonishment, shrinks small enough to enter the door. However, she had left the key on a table and is now unable to reach it. She finds and eats a cake labelled "Eat me", which causes her to grow to a tremendous size. Distraught, Alice bursts into tears. As she cries, the White Rabbit rushes past, dropping a fan and gloves. Alice uses the fan to cool herself down, which causes her to shrink once more and leaves her swimming in a pool of her own tears. There she meets various animals and birds, who convene on a bank and engage in a "Caucus Race" to dry themselves. Alice inadvertently frightens the animals away by mentioning her cat.

Mistaking her for his maidservant, the White Rabbit orders Alice to go to his house and retrieve his lost gloves and fan. Alice finds another bottle and drinks from it, causing her to grow to such an extent that she gets stuck in the house. Attempting to extract her, the White Rabbit and his neighbours eventually take to hurling pebbles that turn into small cakes. Alice eats one and shrinks herself, allowing her to flee into the forest. She meets a Caterpillar seated on a mushroom and smoking a hookah. Under the Caterpillar's questioning, Alice begins to admit to her current identity crisis, compounded by her inability to remember a poem. Before crawling away, the Caterpillar says that a bite of one side of the mushroom will make her larger, while a bite from the other side will make her smaller. During a period of trial and error, Alice's neck extends between the treetops, frightening a pigeon who mistakes her for a serpent. After shrinking to an appropriate height, Alice arrives at the home of a Duchess, who owns a perpetually grinning Cheshire Cat. The Duchess's baby, whom she hands to Alice, transforms into a piglet, which Alice releases into the woods. The Cheshire Cat appears to Alice and directs her toward the Hatter and March Hare before disappearing, leaving his grin behind. Alice finds the Hatter, March Hare, and a sleepy Dormouse in the middle of a tea party. The Hatter explains that it is always 6 p.m. (tea time) – the consequence of his having quarrelled with Time. Unable to answer the riddle "Why is a raven like a writing desk?", and considering the company rude, Alice walks off, declaring "It's the stupidest tea-party I ever was at in all my life!"

Noticing a door in a tree, Alice passes through and finds herself back in the room from the beginning of her journey. She takes the key and opens the door to the garden, which turns out to be the croquet court of the Queen of Hearts, whose guard consists of living playing cards. Alice participates in a croquet game, in which hedgehogs are used as balls, flamingos are used as mallets, and soldiers act as hoops. The Queen is short-tempered, constantly ordering beheadings. When the Cheshire Cat's lone head appears, the Queen orders its beheading, an act which appears impossible in the absence of a body from which to sever it. Alice prompts the Queen to release the Duchess, now in prison.
Alice meets a Gryphon and a Mock Turtle, who dance to the Lobster Quadrille while Alice recites (rather incorrectly) a poem. The Mock Turtle sings "Beautiful Soup", during which the Gryphon drags Alice away for a trial, in which the Knave of Hearts stands accused of stealing the Queen's tarts. The trial is conducted by the King of Hearts, and the jury is composed of animals that Alice previously met. Alice gradually grows in size and confidence, allowing herself increasingly frequent remarks on the irrationality of the proceedings. The Queen eventually commands Alice's beheading, but Alice scoffs that her guard is only a pack of playing cards. The cards rise up into the air and come swarming down upon her.
Alice wakes from her dream to find her sister brushing leaves from her face. Alice tells her about her adventures, then runs in for her tea, leaving her sister on the bank to imagine all the curious happenings for herself.

SIGNIFICANCE (themes, reception, legacy: use ONLY for the closing wrap-up, to say why the novel matters):
[Writing style and themes]
Symbolism: Carroll's biographer Morton N. Cohen reads Alice as a roman à clef populated with real figures from Carroll's life. Alice is based on Alice Liddell; the Dodo is Carroll; Wonderland is Oxford; even the Mad Hatter's Tea Party, according to Cohen, is a send-up of Alice's own birthday party. The critic Jan Susina rejects Cohen's account, arguing that Alice the character bears a tenuous relationship with Alice Liddell.
Beyond its refashioning of Carroll's everyday life, Cohen argues, Alice critiques Victorian ideals of childhood. It is an account of "the child's plight in Victorian upper-class society", in which Alice's mistreatment by the creatures of Wonderland reflects Carroll's own mistreatment by older people as a child.
In the eighth chapter, three cards are painting the roses 

[Reception]
Alice was published to critical praise. One magazine declared it "exquisitely wild, fantastic, [and] impossible". In the late 19th century, Walter Besant wrote that Alice in Wonderland "was a book of that extremely rare kind which will belong to all the generations to come until the language becomes obsolete".

No story in English literature has intrigued me more than Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland. It fascinated me the first time I read it as a schoolboy.
F. J. Harvey Darton argued in a 1932 book that Alice ended an era of didacticism in children's literature, inaugurating a new era in which writing for children aimed to "delight or entertain".

scenes.narration_fa: ورود به خانه خرگوش سفید و نوشیدن از بطری دیگری باعث شد که او دوباره به شدت بزرگ شود و این بار در خانه گیر بیفتد. برای بیرون آوردن او، همسایگان و White Rabbit شروع به پرتاب سنگریزه‌هایی کردند که به کیک‌های کوچکی تبدیل می‌شدند. با خوردن یکی از آن‌ها، Alice دوباره کوچک شد و توانست به داخل جنگل بگریزد. در آنجا او با Caterpillar مواجه شد که روی یک قارچ نشسته بود و قلیان می‌کشید.
scenes.source_en: Alice finds another bottle and drinks from it, causing her to grow to such an extent that she gets stuck in the house. Attempting to extract her, the White Rabbit and his neighbours eventually take to hurling pebbles that turn into small cakes. Alice eats one and shrinks herself, allowing her to flee into the forest. She meets a Caterpillar seated on a mushroom and smoking a hookah.
scenes.setting_en: A dark green forest with large mushrooms.
scenes.action_en: Alice talks to a blue Caterpillar sitting on a red mushroom smoking a hookah.

beat_visuals.visual_en: Alice grows extremely large inside a small rustic cottage, her arm bursting out of the living room window while terrified woodland animals watch from the yard outside.
Alice eats a magical small cake on the grass outside the cottage, rapidly shrinking in size as pebble-turned cakes scatter across the dirt path near the forest.
Alice stands in a dense magical forest looking up at the Caterpillar, who sits comfortably on a tall red spotted mushroom smoking a long wooden hookah pipe.

scenes.narration_fa: زیر پرسش‌های Caterpillar، او به بحران هویت خود اعتراف کرد و نتوانست شعر مورد نظر را به یاد بیاورد. پیش از خزیدن به نقطه‌ای دیگر، Caterpillar به او گفت که یک سمت قارچ او را بزرگ‌تر و سمت دیگرش او را کوچک‌تر می‌کند. پس از کمی تلاش و خطا، گردن Alice تا بالای درختان امتداد یافت و کبوتری را که او را با مار اشتباه گرفته بود ترساند. بعد از بازگشت به اندازه مناسب، او به خانه یک Duchess رسید که صاحب یک Cheshire Cat با لبخند همیشگی بود.
scenes.source_en: Under the Caterpillar's questioning, Alice begins to admit to her current identity crisis, compounded by her inability to remember a poem. Before crawling away, the Caterpillar says that a bite of one side of the mushroom will make her larger, while a bite from the other side will make her smaller. During a period of trial and error, Alice's neck extends between the treetops, frightening a pigeon who mistakes her for a serpent. After shrinking to an appropriate height, Alice arrives at the home of a Duchess, who owns a perpetually grinning Cheshire Cat.
scenes.setting_en: A deep woodland filled with tall trees and oversized plants.
scenes.action_en: Alice stands among giant trees with a grinning cat watching from a branch above.
scenes.mood_en: Surreal and mysterious with soft daylight.

beat_visuals.visual_en: The Caterpillar blows a thick ring of smoke into the air while sitting atop a red mushroom in the deep green forest, surrounded by tall ferns and moss.
Alice stretches her long neck high up through the green treetops of the forest, frightening a startled gray pigeon that flies away from its leafy nest.
Alice stands in front of a rustic stone cottage in the woods, looking up at the Cheshire Cat whose purple and pink striped body rests on a tree branch.

scenes.narration_fa: کودک Duchess در دستان Alice به یک خوک کوچک تبدیل شد و او حیوان را در جنگل آزاد کرد. سپس Cheshire Cat ظاهر شد و او را پیش از ناپدید شدن به سوی Hatter و March Hare هدایت کرد. در آنجا او Hatter و March Hare را به همراه یک Dormouse خواب‌آلود در میان یک مهمانی چای پیدا کرد. Hatter توضیح داد که زمان همیشه روی ساعت شش عصر متوقف مانده است چون او با Time دعوایش شده بود. از پاسخ دادن به معما بازماند و گروه را بی‌ادب یافت، پس با جمله‌ای تند مهمانی چای را ترک کرد.
scenes.source_en: The Duchess's baby, whom she hands to Alice, transforms into a piglet, which Alice releases into the woods. The Cheshire Cat appears to Alice and directs her toward the Hatter and March Hare before disappearing, leaving his grin behind. Alice finds the Hatter, March Hare, and a sleepy Dormouse in the middle of a tea party. The Hatter explains that it is always 6 p.m. (tea time) – the consequence of his having quarrelled with Time. Unable to answer the riddle, and considering the company rude, Alice walks off, declaring it's the stupidest tea party she ever was at.
scenes.setting_en: A long outdoor table set with teacups under the trees.
scenes.action_en: Alice walks away from a tea table while a grinning cat head floats nearby.
scenes.mood_en: Absurd and whimsical with warm afternoon light.

beat_visuals.visual_en: Alice holds a small pink piglet in her arms outside a rustic cottage, while the Cheshire Cat hovers in the air above, leaving only a wide grinning smile behind.
The Hatter and the March Hare sit at a long outdoor tea table cluttered with teacups and teapots, while a sleepy dormouse slumbers between them under lanterns.
Alice turns away in annoyance and walks down a forest path, leaving behind a messy outdoor tea party with empty chairs, teacups, and a sleeping dormouse.

scenes.narration_fa: از طریق دری که روی یک درخت قرار داشت، او دوباره به همان اتاق آغاز سفر خود بازگشت. او کلید را برداشت و در را به سوی باغ گشود که در واقع زمین بازی کریکت Queen of Hearts بود. در این بازی عجیب، جوجه‌تیغی‌ها به عنوان توپ، فلامینگوها به عنوان چوب بازی و سربازان به عنوان حلقه استفاده می‌شدند. ملکه بسیار تندخو بود و مدام فرمان گردن‌زدن صادر می‌کرد. هنگامی که سر Cheshire Cat پدیدار شد، ملکه دستور داد او را گردن بزنند در حالی که بدنی وجود نداشت تا سر از آن جدا شود.
scenes.source_en: Noticing a door in a tree, Alice passes through and finds herself back in the room from the beginning of her journey. She takes the key and opens the door to the garden, which turns out to be the croquet court of the Queen of Hearts, whose guard consists of living playing cards. Alice participates in a croquet game, in which hedgehogs are used as balls, flamingos are used as mallets, and soldiers act as hoops. The Queen is short-termpered, constantly ordering beheadings. When the Cheshire Cat's lone head appears, the Queen orders its beheading, an act which appears impossible in the absence of a body.
scenes.setting_en: A manicured royal garden with hedge walls.
scenes.action_en: Alice plays croquet using a flamingo as a mallet while the angry Queen of Hearts watches.
scenes.mood_en: Tense and royal with bright contrasting colors.

beat_visuals.visual_en: Alice opens a small wooden door set into the trunk of a giant forest tree, revealing a bright green garden filled with sculpted rose bushes and playing card guards.
The Queen of Hearts stands furiously on a green lawn holding a flamingo mallet, pointing a stern finger at living playing card soldiers on a croquet court.
The Queen of Hearts yells in anger at the floating head of the Cheshire Cat, which grinds its wide smile in the air above a croquet court filled with rose bushes.

scenes.narration_fa: در ادامه، Alice با یک Gryphon و یک Mock Turtle دیدار کرد که به همراه هم رقصیدند و شعر خواندند. پس از آن، Gryphon او را برای شرکت در یک دادگاه با خود کشاند تا محاکمه Knave of Hearts را تماشا کند. این دادگاه به اتهام دزدیدن تارت‌های ملکه به ریاست King of Hearts و با هیئت منصفه‌ای از همان حیوانات پیشین برگزار شد. با افزایش اندازه و اعتمادبه‌نفس، Alice مدام به بی‌منقی روند دادگاه اعتراض کرد. ملکه خشمگین دستور گردن‌زدن او را صادر کرد اما او گفت آن‌ها تنها یک دسته ورق بازی بیش نیستند.
scenes.source_en: Alice meets a Gryphon and a Mock Turtle, who dance to the Lobster Quadrille while Alice recites a poem. The Mock Turtle sings, during which the Gryphon drags Alice away for a trial, in which the Knave of Hearts stands accused of stealing the Queen's tarts. The trial is conducted by the King of Hearts, and the jury is composed of animals that Alice previously met. Alice gradually grows in size and confidence, allowing herself increasingly frequent remarks on the irrationality of the proceedings. The Queen eventually commands Alice's beheading, but Alice scoffs that her guard is only a pack of playing cards.
scenes.setting_en: A large courtroom filled with animal jurors and royal guards.
scenes.action_en: Alice stands tall in front of the Queen of Hearts as playing cards rise up around her.

beat_visuals.visual_en: Alice walks through a sunny seaside landscape, watching a mythical gryphon and a mock turtle dance joyfully together near the splashing waves of the blue ocean.
Alice stands inside a crowded courtroom facing a king on a high throne, while a jury of woodland animals sits attentively listening to the dramatic trial proceedings.
Alice grows tall and points defiantly at the angry Queen of Hearts inside a grand courtroom, while a flurry of paper playing cards swirls violently through the air.

scenes.narration_fa: در جمع‌بندی، تمام این رویدادهای شگفت‌انگیز و سفرهای پرماجرا در این داستان به پایان می‌رسند و Alice بیدار می‌شود تا خواهرش را در حال پاک کردن برگ‌ها از روی صورتش ببیند. این اثر بی‌نظیر به عنوان یکی از آثار برجسته ادبیات ویکتوریایی شناخته می‌شود که ساختار و شخصیت‌های آن تأثیر عمیقی بر فرهنگ عامه گذاشته‌اند. این رمان جریان ادبی آموزش‌محور کودکان را دگرگون ساخت و دوره‌ای را آغاز کرد که هدف نوشته‌ها سرگرم کردن و لذت بخشیدن بود. این قصه با منطق بازی می‌کند و با جذابیت پایدار خود همواره زنده باقی می‌ماند.
scenes.source_en: The cards rise up into the air and come swarming down upon her. Alice wakes from her dream to find her sister brushing leaves from her face. Alice tells her about her adventures, then runs in for her tea, leaving her sister on the bank to imagine all the curious happenings for herself. It has become one of the best-known works of Victorian literature; its narrative, structure, characters, and imagery have had a wide influence on popular culture and literature. It is credited as helping end an era of didacticism in children's literature, inaugurating an era in which writing for children aimed to "delight or entertain". The tale plays with logic, giving the story lasting popularity.
scenes.setting_en: The same peaceful riverbank under the trees.
scenes.action_en: Alice wakes up on the grass while her sister gently brushes leaves from her face.

beat_visuals.visual_en: Alice wakes up lying on a green riverbank under a shady tree, blinking her eyes as her sister gently brushes falling autumn leaves away from her face.
A stack of old Victorian storybooks rests on a wooden table next to a steaming porcelain teacup and a delicate silver spoon in a cozy, sunlit English room.
A whimsical fantasy landscape glows under a warm golden sunset, featuring giant mushrooms, a winding river, and floating playing cards drifting through a magical misty forest.
